subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A researcher compares two hepatic carbamoyl phosphate synthetase enzymes. One is mitochondrial, uses free ammonia for ureagenesis, and is allosterically activated by N-acetylglutamate. The other is cytosolic, uses glutamine for de novo pyrimidine synthesis, and is activated by PRPP.
question: Which of the following best distinguishes these two enzymes?

options.text: Only carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I is inhibited by UTP.
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I uses glutamine, whereas the cytosolic enzyme uses free ammonia.
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I is cytosolic, whereas the pyrimidine-synthesis enzyme is mitochondrial.
The pyrimidine-synthesis enzyme requires N-acetylglutamate as an allosteric activator.
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I is activated by N-acetylglutamate, whereas the pyrimidine-synthesis enzyme is activated by PRPP.

explanation_correct: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I is mitochondrial, uses free ammonia for ureagenesis, and requires N-acetylglutamate as an allosteric activator. Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II is cytosolic, uses glutamine for de novo pyrimidine synthesis, and is activated by PRPP and inhibited by UTP.

explanation_incorrect.A: UTP feedback-inhibits the pyrimidine pathway at carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II, not carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I.
explanation_incorrect.B: The substrate use is reversed: carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I uses free ammonia, and carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II uses glutamine.
explanation_incorrect.C: The locations are reversed: carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I is mitochondrial, and carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II is cytosolic.
explanation_incorrect.D: N-acetylglutamate activates carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I; carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II is activated by PRPP and inhibited by UTP.

educationalObjective: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I is the mitochondrial, N-acetylglutamate-activated enzyme of ureagenesis, whereas carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II is the cytosolic, PRPP-activated enzyme of pyrimidine synthesis.
